title: Is game dev now your new "game"? How many are doing it just for fun?
author: HereToLearn321
selftext:
I imagine many are trying to cash in on the "gold rush" . But how  many of you little \_\_\_ are doing it just for the pure fun of making quick little games (or  even large games)?



Anyone just making prototype after prototype and not even putting it online anywhere? Just want to see your little ideas come alive?

comments.author: ABurningDesire
comments.body:
I always wanted to make a game and make my own models. I’ve started using blender to make a model and I’m really enjoying it. It’s so much fun!! 

https://reddit.com/link/1y2lpnq/video/mis9equcz43i1/player

comments.author: Shppo
comments.body: yes - I think I'm addicted

replies.author: No_Degree_8837
replies.body: Me too, replaced crack with gamedev

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: For me its a learning project. I can learn a lot of stuff. Do I dream about making awesome 100 hour game one day? yes but the first game will no manage that. my plan is to release a little free game people enjoy and make many mistakes now so I do not make them later.

comments.author: Muito-Fish123
comments.body:
This is kind of my mentality, I have been working on a concept for 9 months now that merges features from Stellaris and HOI4. Sure I could go and play those games, but there is always a feature or mechanic that you don't really enjoy, so I am taking inspiration and developing those features that I would like to see for my own game. 

About the "gold rush" I think that is just survivorship bias, you only ever hear about successes so it makes game dev seem easy but I would say it's a lonely and hard path, you can pour your heart out for months / years and get nothing in return.

comments.author: Bloodrose_GW2
comments.body: I'm just playing around for the fun of it, making a game together with my daughter, mostly for her.

comments.author: DannySan96
comments.body:
I played around with some personal projects first, just to see where AI capability is at and to figure out good workflows for myself.

Now I am contributing to a cool open source project, which has been really really fun. Just a couple of nerds making their vision come true together, with players actually enjoying what we do.

comments.author: Important-Damage-173
comments.body: Yep. I dont even play any other games. I just test my own stuff then once its 70% done I change my mind and make a new game.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body: The rush is real. It's an oversaturated market now with low barries to entry. Don't expect to make money as a beginner. If anything standards and expectations have risen, and people can spot AI slop more easy. Don't expect to easily find a job either after learning for a bit. If anything game dev jobs were already underpaid before AI. I'd say you need to be medium level at least with general programming experience and education to make any money of it

comments.author: jimbojohndoe
comments.body: Aiming for the money, but even then, it's been one of my dream to do game dev, skill issue is not one of them right now for me so yeah it's been turning to to my fun session. I don't even play video games except my own for testing, so this is turning into my 2nd day +night job. I been working on a couple small games, one big game, and my custom harness app for Claude.

comments.author: PickerLeech
comments.body:
I "made" a few retro game clones, mostly basic racers but novelty wore off as soon as I saw other people's games which are far superior. I don't need the ego rub of creating my clone when others produce far better

I have created one unique game which is more complex than intended. I let Gemini build iterations without me reviewing and now it seems pretty bonafide and complex. Not sure if I'll like it but there's a chance

comments.author: pocipocster
comments.body: Yep

comments.author: richchiudev
comments.body: >Honestly, watching a tiny, silly idea go from a blank screen to something playable feels like pure magic. If you're only in it for a quick cash grab, game dev will burn you out fast anyway—the genuine joy of creating fun little moments is the only thing that keeps you going long-term.

comments.author: AloneButton6264
comments.body: For me, it's just for fun. But the last game I currently developing, turn out to be good (imo) and make me considering to publish to make some money.

comments.author: xsorr
comments.body:
Always wanted to make games when I was young, was one of those i want to be a footballer/police kind of thing, not that dramatic though.

So its nice to be working towards something I like. Andddd I really needed a side/passion project after my last one is about to be wrapped up.

comments.author: ValhallaSun
comments.body:
I have been working on a browser MMORPG for about 2 years, building a complex world with unique mechanics, and I clearly understand that there is no storefront for browser games (such as Steam or Google Play), which means that there is no point in waiting for profit, but I honestly get much more pleasure when I see how players immerse themselves in the world and its possibilities. When they are interested in the plot, or they suggest some ideas that can be implemented and improve the game.  
Gamedev is not always about money.

replies.author: datNovazGG
replies.body: I think you can make an electron app and publish on Steam though? You don't get the best performance that way, but I wouldn't make browser game if it was performance I was looking for so I assume it's fine. However, you're certainly not limited to the browser.

replies.author: ValhallaSun
replies.body: I already thought about it, I also thought about a mobile application and so on, but now in the era of fast endorphins, I'm not sure that many people will like such a game. Let's see what will happen in version V0.1, and thanks for the recommendation =)

comments.author: sixsik6
comments.body: Yep. It's a hobby for me. Always wanted to be in game dev, but I hate the industry and there's no guaranteed money these days. I run my own business which has nothing to do with game dev. I do this for funsies

comments.author: patchwork-engine
comments.body:
I went in doubly so, and I built an AI-first game engine for my needs: [https://github.com/outsidedata/patchwork](https://github.com/outsidedata/patchwork)

Multiplayer native, tons of built-ins.

replies.author: datNovazGG
replies.body: I get 404 on the Github page you've linked too. Is the repo private?

comments.author: The8Darkness
comments.body:
Working on a game that I wanted to make years ago because no game that exists quite fit what I want. A few games that are kinda what I want turned more and more into pay2win and became more and more time consuming (I dont like games that NEED you to play 2+ hours EVERY day)

Still far away from beeing finished, wanted to get to a point where I have nothing to complain about anymore but getting all the little details just right takes forever (been working on it for months and dont expect to be remotely done anytime soon). Then when I am happy first run a closed playtest with a couple friends and then think about a release.

comments.author: Due-Math-4038
comments.body: Im doing it out of fun honestly, im rebuilding a childhood game i played but with updated graphics, mechanics systems and so on and im having a blast just seeing my ideas become reality without any coding experience

comments.author: J0rdian
comments.body: gold rush? what lol

comments.author: TheLastNeonDev
comments.body: started mostly for fun tbh, been at it since june and im on build 170 now. its a game about a neon sign workshop in a 1996 hong kong back lane bc ive been obsessed with hk since chungking express

comments.author: Ok_Dog_7189
comments.body: Yeah it's genuinely fun to have Claude make a custom game lol... Doesn't have to be good or appeal to anyone else, just keep adding mechanics that I like and see what happens

comments.author: Vrigoth
comments.body:
I'm at my 6th prototype. 3 of them have flowered into actually interesting games (I believe).

I'm making games I would've liked to play.

I'll publish them, just to share. If it ends up making money, so be it, but not the goal.

comments.author: BuffaloConscious7919
comments.body: Yup , I procrastinate by over engineering my game

comments.author: dildopants
comments.body: I've been porting games not making them from scratch. It's all I've done for a month now, I love it. I should be playing GTA right now but I'm not!

comments.author: Briskfall
comments.body:
Caught red-handed... 🫣

I'm taking it slow because I wouldn't want something lame that I can't justify out there... 😗💦

comments.author: dr0idattack137
comments.body: For fun but because I wanted to prove out the software factory and get long running dev going across multiple LLMs of different companies and my open weights AI Linux box. And it works. I got a decent game (to me anyhow) in three weeks and I can control with Linear or one master Claude session. I should oss my harness but I’ll do that later lol.

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: i do small AI experiments for the fun of seeing an idea work, but i'm not making games myself

comments.author: Neither_Berry_100
comments.body:
There is no gold rush. Most indie games don't make money. Steam games have 4x overnight recently. History shows us that this does not increase revenue. It suddenly got much harder to make money.

2025 = 20k games. First half of 2026 = 12k games = 24k for the year. Recently = 85k a year effective rate.
